$comment: TrustLens source verification manifest. Produced by the Phase 1 verification pass mandated by DEC-003. Machine-readable companion to docs/01-research/RESEARCH-001-source-inventory.md. Tracking parameters (utm_source) have been stripped from all URLs.
amended: 2026-08-14 (GATE-001) — verified fraction restated as PRIMARY_VERIFIED only; claim_under_test and blocks_rules recorded for the seven failed sources that previously carried neither, so the manual re-retrieval work list is explicit.
verification_method: Automated retrieval (HTTPS GET) followed by targeted claim location within the retrieved document. No claim is graded PRIMARY_VERIFIED unless its specific wording was located in the issuing body's own document.

grades.PRIMARY_VERIFIED: Issuing body's own document retrieved AND the specific claim located within it
grades.PRIMARY_CITED_UNVERIFIED: Specific document cited and shown to exist, but the claim was not locatable in retrieved content
grades.INDEX_ONLY: Citation resolves to a listing or home page, not a document substantiating the claim
grades.RETRIEVAL_FAILED: Document could not be retrieved from this environment; existence and content unconfirmed

summary.$comment_fraction: Only PRIMARY_VERIFIED counts as verified. PRIMARY_CITED_UNVERIFIED (SRC-023) is shown to exist but its claim was not located, so it is excluded from this fraction. Matches RESEARCH-001 section 2.

evidence.claim: UPI PIN must not be shared; only sending money requires UPI PIN.

sources.title: Digital Arrest: The Modern-Day Cyber Scam
verified_quotes: Digital arrest is a scam designed to extort money from victims using fear, deceit, and intimidation. Fraudsters impersonate law enforcement officials, using threats of arrest, frozen bank accounts, and passport cancellations to coerce victims into paying a 'fine' or 'security deposit' to avoid legal action.

Coercion: Victims are threatened with arrest, freezing of bank accounts, or passport cancellation. They are instructed not to involve family or lawyers, and are asked to pay a 'security deposit' or 'fine.'
With fake documents, doctored videos, and even spoofed phone numbers, the scammers create an air of legitimacy
claiming that the victim is involved in serious crimes like money laundering, cybercrime, or drug trafficking
sources.discrepancy: D6 — the source does not use the word 'secrecy'. Its actual wording is 'instructed not to involve family or lawyers'. Encode the source wording, not the paraphrase.
sources.note: Fully verifies the two highest-severity rules in the starter set.

manual_retrieval.review_notes: Update manual retrieval metadata and permit publication subject to existing rule QA.

evidence.claim: 'Scan a QR code to receive money' is fraudulent when it is coupled with UPI PIN entry; QR+PIN is a payment act, not a receipt act.
